		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;">by </font><font style="display: inline;">19% for 2013 and 39% for 2012.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The decrease of 3% in 2014 was primarily due to the reduction of new customers in the third quarter of 2014, which was</font><font style="display: inline;"> due to various factors</font><font style="display: inline;">, including</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">o</font><font style="display: inline;">ur planned reduction in marketing spend in the second and third quarters of 2014 during the 2014 World Cup</font><font style="display: inline;">, which</font><font style="display: inline;"> adversely impacted our new customer conversion rates for longer than we estimated. In addition, the weakening Indian Rupee during the six months ended September 30, 2013 resulted in higher rates of new customer growth in the same period in the prior year as compared to the current year. In the third quarter of 2014, we also faced new and aggressive pricing competition in our major recipient countries.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cost Per Acquisition of a Gross Additional Customer. </font><font style="display: inline;">We calculate cost per acquisition of a gross additional customer</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">in a reporting period as direct marketing cost, a portion of which is reflected in our cost of revenue, divided by gross additional customers added in a given period. Our direct marketing cost does not include certain indirect marketing costs that are included in our marketing expense line item in our consolidated statements of operations. Examples of our indirect marketing costs include personnel-related costs, including stock-based compensation and creative production costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cost Per Acquisition of a New Customer</font><font style="display: inline;">. We calculate cost per acquisition of a new customer, in a reporting period as direct marketing cost, a portion of which is reflected in our cost of revenue, divided by new customers added in a given period. Our direct marketing cost does not include certain indirect marketing costs that are included in our marketing expense line item in our consolidated statements of operations. Examples of our indirect marketing costs include personnel-related costs, including stock-based compensation and creative production costs.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The direct marketing costs are used to acquire both new customers and win-back customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="display: inline;">. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure that we calculate as net income (loss) adjusted for provision for income taxes, interest expense, interest income, </font><font style="display: inline;">amortization of acquired intangible, depreciation and other amortization</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> stock-based compensation</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">business e-mail compromise fraud loss</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Depreciation and other amortization expense includes impairment charges related to long-lived assets </font><font style="display: inline;">primarily </font><font style="display: inline;">due to the relocation of our corporate headquarters during the third quarter of 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">For a reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA to net income (loss) and an explanation of how management uses this metric, see &#x201C;Selected Financial Data.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Basis of Presentation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue. </font><font style="display: inline;">We generate revenue from transaction fees charged to customers, and foreign exchange spreads on transactions where the payout currency is other than U.S. dollars. Our revenue is derived from each transaction and may vary based on the size of the transaction, the funding method used, the currency to ultimately be disbursed and the country to which the funds are transferred. Revenue is recognized when we accept the transaction for processing, net of cancellations and refunds. Revenue growth will depend on our ability to retain </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">existing</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> active</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> customer</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and grow</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> our</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> active customer</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> base by attracting more</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> gross additional customers</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cost of Revenue. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our cost of revenue includes </font><font style="display: inline;">fees paid to disbursement partners fo</font><font style="display: inline;">r paying funds to the recipient or for paying bills to </font><font style="display: inline;">utility providers</font><font style="display: inline;">, provision</font><font style="display: inline;"> for transaction losses</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> fees paid to payment processors for funding transactions</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> the costs of certain promotional activities to acquire gross additional customers</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">including</font><font style="display: inline;"> referees </font><font style="display: inline;">as </font><font style="display: inline;">described below under &#x201C;&#x2014;Marketing Expense.&#x201D; We expect our cost of revenue to increase on an absolute basis for the foreseeable future as we continue to grow our business.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Marketing Expense. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our marketing expense </font><font style="display: inline;">is </font><font style="display: inline;">comprised</font><font style="display: inline;"> of business development, </font><font style="display: inline;">offline</font><font style="display: inline;">, online and promotional advertising costs to acquire </font><font style="display: inline;">and retain </font><font style="display: inline;">customers, employee compensation and related costs to support the marketing process and allocated facilities and other supporting overhead costs. </font><font style="display: inline;">We have</font><font style="display: inline;"> a Refer-A-Friend incentive program where the referrer receives either a cash-type or non-cash award and the referee receives a non-cash award. Cash-type awards are considered to be cash-type because the referrer could use them as cash</font><font style="display: inline;"> and are classified as </font><font style="display: inline;">marketing </font><font style="display: inline;">expense</font><font style="display: inline;">. The amount related to the referee is classified as cost of revenue for non-cash awards. Awards provided to the referrer are recorded in marketing expense as these payments are </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">56</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display: inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;">a reward for bringing a new customer to Xoom. We anticipate our marketing expense will vary from period to period due to the timing</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and nature</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">of</font><font style="display: inline;"> such</font><font style="display: inline;"> programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Technology and Development Expense. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our technology and development expense consists of employee compensation and related costs for our engineers and developers based in the United States and Guatemala, costs associated with professional services and consulting, development of new technologies, enhancements of existing technologies, amortization of capitalized internally-developed software and the intangible asset (developed technology) acquired in the </font><font style="display: inline;">a</font><font style="display: inline;">cquisition</font><font style="display: inline;"> of BlueKite</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> LTD, or the Acquisition</font><font style="display: inline;">, and allocated facilities and other supporting overhead costs.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Internally-developed software costs, which primarily relate to the development of </font><font style="display: inline;">new services such as Xoom Bill Pay and </font><font style="display: inline;">enhancements</font><font style="display: inline;"> to products</font><font style="display: inline;"> such as the Xoom App, are a combination of internal compensation costs of engineering time and costs of outside consultants.</font><font style="display: inline;"> We intend to continue to invest in technology and development efforts to further improve our customer experience and to continue expanding our operating platform. As a result, we expect technology and development expense to increase on an absolute basis for the foreseeable future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Customer Service and Operations Expense</font><font style="display: inline;">. Our customer service and operations expense consists of </font><font style="display: inline;">costs incurred for </font><font style="display: inline;">outsourced </font><font style="display: inline;">support</font><font style="display: inline;"> centers, employee compensation for our employees who support customer service calls, costs incurred for fraud detection, compliance operations, maintenance costs related to our outsourced </font><font style="display: inline;">support</font><font style="display: inline;"> centers and allocated facilities and other supporting overhead costs. We expect customer service and operations expense to increase on an absolute basis for the foreseeable future to support the anticipated growth of our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">General and Administrative Expense. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our general and administrative expense consists of employee compensation and related costs for our executives, finance, legal, compliance policy, human resources and other administrative employees, outside consulting, legal and accounting services and facilities and other supporting overhead costs not allocated to other departments. We expect to incur additional expenses </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for the foreseeable future </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">to support our continuing growth</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Business E-mail Compromise Fraud Loss</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We were the victim of a criminal fraud during the latter half of December 2014, which we detected on December 30, 2014. The fraud, known to law enforcement authorities as business e-mail compromise, or BEC, fraud involved employee impersonation and fraudulent requests targeting our finance department, which resulted in the transfer of $30.8 million in corporate cash to overseas accounts. As a result, we recorded an expense of $30.8 million in the fourth quarter of 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our Board of Directors authorized an independent investigation into the matter, led by outside </font><font style="display: inline;">legal counsel</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;The investigation concluded on February </font><font style="display: inline;">17</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2015.&nbsp;The investigation uncovered no evidence that our systems, including our operational, security and proprietary risk management systems were penetrated or that any corporate information, including our financial and account information, was accessed. In addition, there was no evidence of any impact to any customer data or customer funds. </font><font style="display: inline;">The investigation found no evidence of employee</font><font style="display: inline;"> criminal</font><font style="display: inline;"> involvement in the </font><font style="display: inline;">fraud</font><font style="display: inline;">. We have implemented enhanced internal control procedures as a result of the fraud and are in the process of implementing additional procedures and controls pursuant to recommendations from the investigation. While the fraud will result in some additional near-term expenses, we do not expect it to otherwise have a material impact on its business. We continue to work with federal law enforcement authorities who are actively pursuing a multi-agency criminal investigation. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Expense. </font><font style="display: inline;">Interest expense represents interest incurred in connection with our line of credit and amortization of commitment and arrangement fees.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Income. </font><font style="display: inline;">Interest income represents interest earned on our cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Income (Expense). </font><font style="display: inline;">Other income (expense) consists of gains and/or losses on foreign currency balances due to fluctuations in exchange rates between the initiation of a transaction and the settlement of the transaction (usually a period of no longer than 24 hours).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Provision for Income Taxes.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">P</font><font style="display: inline;">rovision for income taxes consists of state income taxes in the United States and foreign taxes.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have not been required to pay U.S. federal income taxes to date because of our current and accumulated net operating losses which totaled $</font><font style="display: inline;">94.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since inception, we have only been required to pay minimal state income taxes. As of December 31, 2014, we have a full valuation allowance against our deferred tax asset</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">. We continue to assess the need for a valuation allowance on the deferred tax asset</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> by evaluating both positive and negative evidence that may exist. Significant judgment is required in making this assessment, and it is very difficult to predict when our assessment may conclude that the deferred tax asset</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">are</font><font style="display: inline;"> realizable. Based on historical and projected operating performance, we believe that it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be realized in subsequent quarters. We may partially or fully release the deferred tax valuation allowance in a future period to the extent we expect that our operations will generate sufficient taxable income in future periods. Any adjustment to the deferred tax asset valuation allowance will be recorded in the income statement of the period in which the adjustment is determined to be required.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For 2014, tax expense was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$44,769</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, which consisted of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$15,364</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of U.S. state income taxes and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$29,405</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of foreign income taxes.&nbsp;&nbsp;For 2013, tax expense was $37,000, which consisted of U.S. state income taxes.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2014 Compared to 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Revenue increased </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$36.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">30%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013. The increase was primarily due to a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">21</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">% increase in active customers, which included </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">554,543</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">gross additional</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> customers added during 2014. Revenue grew at a faster rate than the increase in our active customers because the annual revenue per average active customer increased from $133 in 2013 to $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">136</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in 2014, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%. This increase was due to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">an increase in average number of transactions per active customer in 2014 as compared to 2013</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2013 Compared to 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Revenue increased $42.2 million, or 53%, in 2013 as compared to 2012. The increase was primarily due to a 36% increase in active customers, which included </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">543,555</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">gross additional</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> customers added during 2013. Revenue grew at a faster rate than the increase in our active customers because the annual revenue per average active customer increased from $124 in 2012 to $133 in 2013, or 8%. This increase was due to changes in the mix of countries we serve toward those with a higher average transaction amount.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2014 Compared to 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Cost of revenue increased </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$7.3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">19%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013. The increase in co</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">st of revenue was driven by a $6.3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million increase in processing and disbursement costs to support the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">28</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">% increase in transactions and a $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million increase in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">promotional advertising spend</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. This was partially offset by a decrease of $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">transaction losses</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">due to lower </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">customer </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">fraud</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ACH</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">loss</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">es</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The decrease in cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue and corresponding increase in gross</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> profit for 2014 was primarily a result of a reduction in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">transaction losses</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2013 Compared to 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Cost of revenue increased $11.3 million, or 42%, in 2013 as compared to 2012. The increase in cost of revenue was driven by a $6.4 million increase to $22.7 million in processing and disbursement costs to support the 51% increase in transactions and a $5.9 million increase to $13.6 million in transaction losses due to the increase in our GSV. This was partially offset by a decrease of $0.9 million in costs related to Refer-A-Friend and other incentive programs. The decrease in cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue and corresponding increase in gross profit for 2013 was primarily a result of a reduction in Refer-A-Friend costs due to a reduction in the reward amount per new user and a result of a reduction in disbursement costs per transaction due to changes in the mix of countries we serve toward those with lower disbursement costs per transaction.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase was driven by </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$4.5 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">related</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to an expansion of our marketing programs to drive increased acquisition</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of gross additional customers</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, including increas</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> television, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">offline and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> online promotions</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> In addition, there was an increase of $</font><font inline;color:#000000;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$0.3 million in professional consulting fees and $0.3 million in allocated rent, asset depreciation </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">expenses and asset impairment charges primarily due to the relocation of our corporate headquarters</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">remaining $0.2 million is primarily due to </font><font style="display: 		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2013 Compared to 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Marketing expense increased $4.4 million, or 21%, in 2013 as compared to 2012. The increase was primarily due to an expansion of our marketing programs to drive increased </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">acquisition of gross additional </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">customer</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, including increasing television, out-of-home, online and incentive promotions by $3.5 million to $21.4 million during 2013. In addition, there was an increase of $0.6 million in personnel-related costs (including stock-based compensation). As a percentage of revenue, marketing expense fluctuates from period to period due to the timing of marketing programs and incentive programs to acquire </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">gross additional</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">customers.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;text-indent:24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2014 Compared to 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Technology and development expense increased </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$14.5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">65%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase was primarily the result of an increase in personnel-related costs of $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million (including stock-based compensation) due to an increase in the U.S. employee headcount to expand and improve our service, and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">an increase in personnel-related costs of $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">(including stock-based compensation) </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">related to our new development center in Guatemala. In </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">addition, there was an increase of $1.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in information technology and infrastructure costs, including </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">increased spend on web hosting services.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> There was also an increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of $1.2 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in asset depreciation and other amortization expense</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> primarily due to the new office space</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, an increase of $1.1 million in allocated </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">rent</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and an increase of $0.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in amortization of acquired intangibles. In addition, there was also an allocation of $0.2 million for asset impairment charges </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">primarily </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">due to the relocation of our corporate headquarters. The remaining increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of $0.8 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">was primarily due to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">other operational spend</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, including</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">increased travel</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2013 Compared to 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Technology and development expense increased $6.5 million, or 41%, in 2013 as compared to 2012. The increase was primarily the result of an increase in personnel-related costs of $4.3 million to $17.2 million (including stock-based compensation) due to an increase in headcount to expand and improve our service. The remaining increase was due to an increase in facilities, information technology and other infrastructure costs of $0.9 million, an increase in depreciation and amortization expense of $0.7 million due to various software projects that were put into service in 2013, including mobile app and text messaging, and an increase in allocated insurance costs of $0.3 million.</font>
		</p>

style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase was primarily due to an increase in the volume of transactions we processed, resulting in an increase of $1.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in costs </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">associated with our outsourced support centers (including communi</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">cation and software costs), $1.3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in personnel-related costs (including 			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2014 Compared to 2013.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> General and administrative expense increased </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$7.8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">59%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in 2014 as compared to 2013. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase was primarily the result of an increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in personnel-related costs of $4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.7 million (including stock-based compensation) due to an increase in headcount to support our overall growth, a $1.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in allocated rent, asset depreciation and asset impairment charges due to the relocation of our corporate headquarters, an increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of $0.5 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in consulting, professional services and public company costs, an increase </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0.4 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in franchise taxes and </font><font style="display: &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The remaining $0.6 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">million increase was primarily due to an increase in information technology, infrastructure costs and other operational spend, including increased travel.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2013 Compared to 2012.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> General and administrative expense increased $4.0 million, or 44%, in 2013 as compared to 2012. The increase was primarily the result of an increase in personnel-related costs of $2.8 million (including stock-based compensation) due to an increase in headcount to support our overall growth, and an increase in consulting, professional services and public company costs of $0.6 million. The remaining $0.6 million increase was due to an increase in facilities, allocated insurance costs, information technology and other infrastructure costs.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">With the exception of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">three months ended September 30</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 2013,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> 2013 and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">September 30</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, we have </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">experienced sequential revenue growth in all periods presented as a result of attracting </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">gross additional</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> customers and retaining our active customers. The sequential decline in revenue in the three months ended September 30, 2013 was due to an unprecedented 38% quarter over quarter</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> increase in revenue during the three months ended June 30, 2013. Revenue was flat between September 30, 2013 and December 31, 2013 due to lower revenue from Indian customers as discussed below. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We experience some seasonal trends in our business. Generally, revenue in our second and fourth quarters is stronger due to Mother&#x2019;s Day and Christmas when we tend to have an increased rate of activity from our active customers. In addition, some of our customers transact more depending on the value of the local currency relative to the U.S. dollar. We see this trend most clearly among our Indian customers, a subset of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">which is highly influenced by the value, or the perceived value, of the Indian Rupee relative to the U.S. dollar. For example, we saw an increase in activity in the three months ended June 30, 2013 and September 30, 2013 due to a weakening Indian Rupee, or the perception of a weakening Indian Rupee. Conversely</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, during the three months ended December 31, 2013, we saw a decrease in activity to India due to a strengthening Indian Rupee, or the perception of a strengthening Indian Rupee.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Indian Rupee </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">volatility in 2014 was not as significant as compared to 2013. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our cost of revenue has increased in absolute dollars but has decreased as a percentage of revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Our operating expenses have increased in absolute dollars as we continue to invest in service innovation and technology by hiring </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">additional employees and continue to introduce new marketing programs to increase brand awareness. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Technology and development became our largest operating expense </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">as a percentage of revenue in 2014 because</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> we acquired BlueKite, LTD to augment our product and development team</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">invested </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in the development</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and launch</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">new service,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Xoom B</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ill </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">P</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ay</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and continued </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">enhancing our mobile products</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">also </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">continue to look for innovative and efficient marketing efforts and expect that our marketing expense will </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">continue to increase and will </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">vary from period to period due to the timing and nature of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">marketing</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> programs.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> In addition, our</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> facilities costs </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">have </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">increased</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> due to our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">new </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">corporate headquarters</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Since inception, we have financed our </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">operations and capital expenditures</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> primarily</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> through the sale of preferred and common stock and, to a lesser extent, from borrowings and exercise </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of stock options to purchase common stock. Our principal uses of cash are funding our operations and capital expenditures.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had cash, cash equivalents, disbursement prefunding and short-term investments of $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">250.2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, which consisted of cash, money market funds, U.S. government securities, </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We hold cash at foreign financial institutions in order to prefund our disbursement partners. Our policy is generally to have relationships with multiple foreign institutions in each of our major markets so that our institutional risk is diversified</font><font style="display: inline;">. For example, we hold balances at eight different</font><font style="display: inline;"> institutions in the Philippines </font><font style="display: inline;">and three large banks</font><font style="display: inline;"> in India</font><font style="display: inline;">, including HDFC Bank Limited</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Punjab National Bank</font><font style="display: inline;">. We generally review financial statements of our disbursement partners before commencing a business relationship with</font><font style="display: inline;"> them, and annually thereafter, though such reviews may not mitigate all risk of loss. Certain of our balances in domestic and all of our balances in foreign institutions are uninsured. Our institutional losses </font><font style="display: inline;">of pre-funded</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">balances</font><font style="display: inline;"> have totaled less than $150,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> since our inception.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We experience significant day-to-day fluctuations in our cash and cash equivalents, disbursement prefunding and line of credit balances. These fluctuations are primarily due to:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:30pt;"><p style="width:30pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:11pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Fluctuations in daily GSV</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. As daily GSV increases, our cash and disbursement prefunding amounts will increase, and we may draw down on our line of credit to fund the increased activit</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ies</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Typically our cash</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and disbursement prefunding balances at period end represent one to four days of disbursements to be made in the subsequent period; and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:30pt;"><p style="width:30pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 6pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:11pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 6pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Timing of period end</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. For periods that end on a weekend or a bank holiday, our cash and cash equivalents and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">disbursement </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">prefunding typically will be more than for periods ending on a weekday as we fund these balances five days a week, but we disburse funds seven days a week.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">If a period ends on a weekend or holiday, our cash, cash equivalents and disbursement prefunding is generally higher than if the period ends on a business day, because we will then prefund our disbursement partners for the entire weekend or through the holiday instead of for one business day. As a result, we would need to draw down on our line of credit discussed below under &#x201C;&#x2014;Our Indebtedness,&#x201D; which would increase our cash, cash equivalents and disbursement prefunding balances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations, and the available borrowing amount under our line of credit will be sufficient to meet our working capital needs and planned capital expenditures for at least the next 12 months. From time to time, we may </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">explore additional financing sources which could include equity, equity-linked and debt financing arrangements. We cannot assure you that any additional financing will be available to us on acceptable terms or at all.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Our Indebtedness</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In October 2009, we entered into a line of credit agreement, or the Loan Agreement, with Silicon Valley Bank, or SVB, which was amended in September 2012 to add a second lender and increase the available borrowing amount. In September 2013, we amended and restated our line of credit by entering into an Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, or the Restated Loan Agreement. The Restated Loan Agreement added additional lenders and increased the available borrowing amount to $150.0 million through September 2016.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We are</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> required to repay the</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">outstanding principal balance under the line of credit in full at least once every eight business days.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Under the Restated Loan Agreement, the interest rate is the greater of prime plus 1.00%, </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;">the federal funds effective rate plus 1.50%, or 4.25%, and we pay a fee of 0.50% per annum for the daily unused portion of the line of credit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have $15.0 million reserved under a standby letter of credit which satisfies the additional collateral requirement to maintain our India operations and a $3.9 million letter of credit issued as a security deposit for our </font><font style="display: inline;">corporate headquarters&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">office lease in January 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2014, </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;"> had $103.1 million available under </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> $150.0 million line of credit, reflecting $28.0 million outstanding under the line of credit and $18.9 million reserved under the two standby letters </font><font style="display: inline;">of credit.</font><font style="display: inline;"> We repaid</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">$28.0 million </font><font style="display: inline;">of borrowing in the first week of January</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2015.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Due to the </font><font style="display: inline;">business e-mail compromise fraud loss</font><font style="display: inline;"> discussed </font><font style="display: inline;">above</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> under &#x201C;&#x2014;Basis of Presentation,&#x201D; </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">were unable to meet one of our debt covenants under the Restated Loan Agreement as of December 31, 2014, and our inability to do so was waived by our lenders who also agreed not to include the amount of the </font><font style="display: inline;">business e-mail compromise fraud loss</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the determination of our compliance with our debt covenants going forward.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cash Flows</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We typically prefund our disbursement partners on each business day which allows the funds to be made available to our disbursement partners seconds or minutes after a customer&#x2019;s transaction is processed. Our prefunding estimates are based on historical experiences with our customers and disbursement partners, which vary depending on factors such as seasonality, the timing of bank holidays, weekends and paydays. These estimates incorporate assumptions surrounding the timing in which the customer funds receivables are settled and the customer liabilities are paid out. We have in the past and could in the future utilize our line of credit to satisfy short-term capital requirements over weekends or during bank holiday periods or high volume sending periods. </font><font style="display: inline;">We are</font><font style="display: inline;"> required to repay the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">outstanding principal balance under the line of credit in full at least once every eight business days.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We typically pay down the outstanding amount on the line of credit the first business day after the weekend or bank holiday period. Given these factors, we believe it is useful to review our cash flow in the aggregate to better understand the short-term flow of funds which can vary greatly depending on the timing of a weekend or bank holiday.</font>
		</p>

As described in &#x201C;&#x2014;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#x201D; above, we utilized the line of credit to prefund disbursement partners </font><font style="display: inline;">partly </font><font style="display: inline;">due </font><font style="display: inline;">to a banking holiday</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">in most of the disbursement countries</font><font style="display: inline;"> following the end of December 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">partly due to </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">reduced </font><font style="display: inline;">cash</font><font style="display: inline;"> balance </font><font style="display: inline;">as a result of the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">business e-mail compromise fraud loss</font><font style="display: inline;"> discussed</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">above under &#x201C;&#x2014;Basis of Presentation.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash provided by financing activities in 2013 was $157.1 million primarily due to $88.4 million net proceeds from our </font><font style="display: inline;">initial public offering, or </font><font style="display: inline;">IPO</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $104.8 million net proceeds from our follow-on offering. This was partially offset by net repayments of $40.0 million under our line of credit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash provided by financing activities in 2012 was $13.6 million consisting primarily of net borrowings of $13.5 million on our line of credit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As described in &#x201C;&#x2014;Our Indebtedness&#x201D; above, SVB issued a standby letter of credit for $15.0 million which satisfies the additional collateral requirement to maintain our India operations. </font><font style="display: inline;">In connection with our corporate headquarters&#x2019; lease arrangement entered into in December 2013, SVB issued a $3.9 million letter of credit in January 2014 as a security deposit for our office lease. </font><font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2014 and 2013, we had $</font><font style="display: inline;">18.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $15.0 million reserved under our</font><font style="display: inline;"> standby</font><font style="display: inline;"> letters of credit, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with </font><font style="display: inline;">U.S. </font><font style="display: inline;">GAAP. The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and related disclosures. We evaluate our estimates and assumptions on an ongoing basis. Our estimates are based on historical experience and various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances. Our actual results could differ from these estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We believe that the assumptions and estimates associated with our income taxes and stock-based compensation have the greatest potential impact on our consolidated financial statements. Therefore, we consider these to be our critical accounting policies and estimates. For further information on all of our significant accounting policies, please see Note </font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">of the accompanying notes to our consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We use the asset and liability method to account for income taxes, which requires the recognition of deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future income tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements or tax returns. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized based on temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts and the tax bases of assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates in effect in the years in which the temporary differences are expected to reverse. We record a valuation allowance to reduce deferred tax asset to the amount that is believed more likely than not to be realized based on analyses of a number of factors including our historical performance, future profitability, expansion plans and future investments in our technologies. As of December 31, 2014, our deferred tax assets were offset in full by a valuation allowance because of the factors above. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We also provide reserves as necessary for uncertain tax positions taken on our tax filings. First, we determine if a tax position is more likely than not to be sustained upon audit solely based on technical merits, including resolution of related appeals or litigation processes, if any. Second, based on the largest amount of benefit, which is more likely than not to be realized on ultimate settlement, we recognize any such differences as a liability. We include in income tax expense any interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions. For all years presented, there are no uncertain tax positions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Stock-based compensation is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as </font><font style="display: inline;">expense, net of estimated forfeitures, over the requisite service period, which is the vesting period of the respective award. </font><font style="display: inline;">As t</font><font style="display: inline;">he</font><font style="display: inline;"> forfeit</font><font style="display: inline;">ure rates</font><font style="display: inline;"> used to calculate stock-based compensation expense</font><font style="display: inline;"> were</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">based on </font><font style="display: inline;">our historical experience</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">f actual</font><font style="display: inline;"> forfeitures differ significantly from our estimates, stock-based compensation expense and our results of operations could be materially impacted.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Determining the fair value of stock-based awards at the grant date requires judgment. </font><font style="display: inline;">We estimate the expense for restricted stock units based on grant date fair value of our common stock. </font><font style="display: inline;">We use the Black-Scholes option-pricing model to determine the fair value of stock options. The determination of the grant date fair value of options using an option-pricing model is affected by our </font><font style="display: inline;">estimated common stock fair value</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as assumptions regarding a number of other complex and subjective variables. These variables include the </font><font style="display: inline;">fair value of our common stock</font><font style="display: inline;">, our expected stock price volatility over the expected term of the o</font><font style="display: inline;">ptions, stock </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">70</font>

		</p>

			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Risk-free rate</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield in effect at the time of the grant for zero-coupon U.S. Treasury notes with remaining terms similar to the expected term of the options.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 6pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Dividend yield</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. We have never declared or paid any cash dividends and do not presently plan to pay cash dividends in the foreseeable future. Consequently, we used an expected dividend yield of zero.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">If any of the assumptions used in the Black-Scholes model changes significantly, stock-based compensation for future awards may differ materially compared with the awards granted previously.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On May 28, 2014, the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Financial Accounting Standards Board </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">issued ASU No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, which requires an entity to recognize the amount of revenue to which it expects to be entitled for the transfer of promised goods or services to customers. The ASU will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective. The new standard is effective for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">us</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> on January 1, 2017. Early application is not permitted. The standard permits the use of either the retrospective or cumulative effect transition method. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We are</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> evaluating the effect that ASU 2014-09 will have on </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">consolidated financial statements and related disclosures. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We have </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">not yet selected a transition method nor</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> have we</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> determined the effect of the standard on </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">our</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ongoing financial reporting</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 72pt;text-indent:-72pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;">ITEM 7A</font><a name="ITEM7A_350968"></a><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;;font-size: 11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Interest Rate Fluctuation Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments consist of cash, money market funds, U.S. government securities, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and corporate bonds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The primary objective of our investment activities is to preserve principal while maximizing income without significantly increasing risk. Because our cash and cash equivalents </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and short-term investments </font><font style="display: inline;">have a relatively short maturity, our portfolio&#x2019;s fair value is relatively insensitive to interest rate changes. We determined that the nominal difference in basis points from potentially investing our cash and cash equivalents </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and short-term investments </font><font style="display: inline;">in longer-term investments did not warrant a change in our investment strategy. In future periods, we will continue to evaluate our investment policy in order to ensure that we continue to meet our overall objectives. We believe a hypothetical 10% increase in interest rates as of December 31, 2014 would have an immaterial impact on our investment portfolio, results of operations and cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Any borrowings under our line of credit with SVB are at a variable rate and, as a result, increases in market interest rates would generally result in increased interest expense on our outstanding borrowings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Foreign Exchange Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We are exposed to foreign exchange risk as we offer our services in </font><font style="display: inline;">32</font><font style="display: inline;"> countries</font><font style="display: inline;"> and disburse our transactions in multiple foreign currencies. However, we believe that this risk is somewhat limited due to the fact that these transactions are usually disbursed in less than three business days. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, we had not entered into any foreign exchange hedging contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Inflation Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:30.95pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We do not believe that inflation has had a material effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. If our costs were to become subject to significant inflationary pressures, we may not be able to fully offset such higher costs through fee increases.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:30.95pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:center;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
